subject.title: fix(memory): search memory and wiki concurrently for corpus=all (#92633)

question: After the code blocker is fixed, should this PR close the linked timeout issue, or should the closing reference be narrowed so https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92647 can own the remaining attribution/debug work?
rationale: This PR addresses additive all-corpus latency, while a separate open PR addresses misleading timeout warning and debug attribution from the same report; automation should not infer the intended issue-closure scope.

options.title: Narrow Closure Scope
options.body: Land this concurrency fix without automatically closing the broader timeout issue until the attribution/debug path is resolved or explicitly split.

options.title: Accept Split Closure
options.body: Treat this PR as closing the central user problem and keep attribution/debug behavior tracked separately in the adjacent PR.

options.title: Pause For Combined Fix
options.body: Hold this PR until concurrency and attribution behavior are coordinated in one merge plan.

recommendation.title: Narrow Closure Scope
recommendation.body: Land this concurrency fix without automatically closing the broader timeout issue until the attribution/debug path is resolved or explicitly split.

likelyOwner.reason: The wiki corpus bridge and memory supplement path history make this the best available owner for deciding split-fix scope.
